chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿUthmān ibn ʿĪsā, from Abī Hilāl, who said:

I asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: “Do nosebleeding, vomiting, and plucking the armpit hair invalidate wudu (ablution)?” He said: “What will you do with this? This is the saying of al-Mughīrah ibn Saʿīd—may Allah curse al-Mughīrah. It is sufficient for you, regarding nosebleeding and vomiting, that you wash it off and do not repeat the wudu (ablution).”

key_terms.الْمُغِيرَةِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ: a figure whose view is being rejected and condemned in this report
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification for salat (prayer)
key_terms.تَغْسِلَهُ: to wash it off, meaning to cleanse the affected impurity
key_terms.لَا تُعِيدَ الْوُضُوءَ: you do not repeat the wudu (ablution)

ai.seo_question: Do nosebleeding or vomiting invalidate wudu (ablution) in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a fiqh ruling on whether nosebleeding, vomiting, and plucking armpit hair invalidate wudu (ablution). Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام rejects this claim, attributes it to al-Mughīrah ibn Saʿīd, and rules that in the case of nosebleeding and vomiting, one only needs to wash away the impurity and does not need to renew wudu (ablution).
